I have been farming these 18 mu for 45 years, and I know every inch of this land. At my age, I cannot do everything by myself anymore, and with my sons working in the factory, I must be careful with labor. Cotton brings good money, but it is back-breaking work—picking and spraying for bollworm never ends. So I will keep only 3 mu of cotton, which my wife and I can manage during the busy season. The remaining 15 mu will stay in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the reliable foundation that feeds the family and brings steady income.

For the winter wheat on those 15 mu, I will rotary till the field before sowing in October and plant an improved local wheat like Shimai—I trust what I know. I will put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer as a base and top-dress with urea at green-up in spring. The well gives me water, so I will irrigate three times: winter irrigation to protect against the cold, once at jointing, and once at heading. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather holds. For pests, I will spray four times—herbicide once and insecticide/fungicide a few more times when I see aphids or rust.

For summer maize, time is everything in June. As soon as the wheat is cut, I will plant hybrid maize with no-tillage—I have learned there is no time to plough, and the crop does fine if I plant quickly. I will apply some compound at sowing and maybe one more dressing when the plants are knee-high. I will irrigate twice, once at sowing if it is dry and once during grain filling. Three pesticide sprays should be enough. I hope for 550 kg per mu.

For the 3 mu of cotton, I will rotary plough in spring and plant an improved variety like Guoxinmian. I will put down basal fertilizer and top-dress once when the plants start flowering. Cotton is thirsty and vulnerable to worms, so I will irrigate twice and spray about 14 times through the season—that is the only way to keep the bollworm away. I expect around 280 kg of seed cotton per mu. That is my plan.
